answer: Submissions that land within 163 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The anchor detector writes to harbor, and wander exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 261 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 26 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
